div.head: Ger 4
div.ab: [4] Ac ic lære, þæt he do, swa ic ær cwæð: gyme ægðer ge ðæs selran ge þæs sæmran, þæt naðor ne misfare, gyf he wealdan mæge, ne corn ne sceaf, ne flæsc ne flotsmeru, ne cyse ne cyslyb, ne nan ðera ðinga ðe æfra to note mæge.

Ac ic lære þæt he do swa ic ær cwæð. gyme ægðer ge ðæs sel|ran. ge þæs sæmran . þæt naðor ne misfare gyf he wealdan mæge . ne corn . ne sceaf . ne flæsc . ne slotsmeru [could be as 17.]. ne cyse . ne cys|lyb. ne nan ðera ðinga ðe æfra to note mæge .

Ac ic lære þæt he do swa ic ær cwæð: gyme ægðer ge ðæs selran ge þæs sæmran þæt naðor ne misfare gyf heealdan mæge, ne corn ne sceaf, ne flæsc ne flotsmeru, ne w cyse ne cyslyb, ne nan ðera ðinga ðe æfra to note mæge.

Vielmehr rath’ ich, dass er handle, wie ich zuvor gesagt habe: er achte sowohl des besseren wie des geringeren, damit weder missrathe, soweit er verfügen kann, Korn noch Garbe, weder Fleisch noch flüssig Fett, weder Käse noch Lab, noch eines der Dinge, die je zu Nutzen [sein] mögen.

Rather I advise that he act as I said before: let him take care of both the better and the poorer, so that nothing goes wrong, as far as he can control it, neither corn nor sheaf, neither meat nor liquid fat [lard or cream-butter], neither cheese nor rennet, nor any of the things that may ever [be] of use.

But I advise that he do just as I said before: take care of both the better and of the worse so that nothing go wrong if he may prevent it; not corn nor sheaf, nor flesh nor morsel of fat, nor cheese nor rennet, nor any of those things which may ever be of note.

But I instruct him to do as I said earlier: care for both the better and the worse so that nothing will go astray if he can prevent it, neither grain nor sheaf, neither meat nor scrap of fat, neither cheese nor rennet, nor any of those things which might ever be of use.
div.note: B's ‘æfra’ stands so. Liebermann compares Gerefa 3 and Gerefa 13, 18.1.
rennet: Literally, “cheese medicine,” the enzymes used to curdle milk into cheese.

note.seg: þa sǽmran ⁊ þa séllan Gedicht Guthlac 463; ‘Kleines wie Grosses’ Sk-Wi
þa sǽmran ⁊ þa séllan poem Guthlac 463; ‘small as well as great’ Sk-Wi

‘floating fat’ Toller; ‘dripping fat’ Sweet; spuma Mätzner s. v. flot; flot mengl.: ‘grease, flüssiges, oben schwimmendes Fett’ Stratman-Bradley. Mittelenglisch stehen nebeneinander: chese, botere, grece and smere; Mätzner s. v. buttere. Agsä. heisst smeoru zwar unguentum, sebum, adeps, nicht ‘Milchfett’; s. jedoch Gl Fett, auch Nord. smjor ‘Fett, Butter’; ferner Mndd. vlot: ‘Sahne’, mengl. flote ‘abrahmen’, flot prov. engl. ‘to skim milk’; daher Kluge hier ‘Rahmbutter’; Sk-Wi: ‘Rahm’

‘floating fat’ Toller; ‘dripping fat’ Sweet; spuma Mätzner s. v. flot; flot ME: ‘grease, liquid fat floating on top’ Stratman-Bradley. In Middle English there stand side by side: chese, botere, grece and smere; Mätzner s. v. buttere. In A.-S. smeoru does indeed mean unguentum, sebum, adeps, not ‘milk-fat’; see, however, Gl Fett, also Norse smjor ‘fat, butter’; further MLG vlot: ‘cream’, ME flote ‘to skim’, flot prov. Engl. ‘to skim milk’; hence Kluge here ‘cream butter’; Sk-Wi: ‘cream’

Unverdaute Milch aus dem Magen säugenden Kalbes oder dieser Magen selbst, ein den Käsestoff der Milch koagulierendes Ferment. [Daneben Hasenmagen verwendet; Cockayne Leechdoms II 376.] Vgl. Gl Käse; cheeselip Wright Dial. Dict.; ‘Quark’ falsch Sk-Wi

Undigested milk from the stomach of a suckling calf, or this stomach itself: a ferment that coagulates the casein of the milk. [Hare’s stomach was also used; Cockayne Leechdoms II 376.] Cf. Gl Käse; cheeselip Wright Dial. Dict.; ‘curd cheese’ wrong Sk-Wi
